package_info.why_malicious: The Codecov Bash Uploader script was surreptitiously modified to include a backdoor that exfiltrates all environment variables and repository configuration from CI/CD environments to a hardcoded external IP address controlled by the attacker. This enabled large-scale supply chain compromise and theft of credentials, tokens, and other secrets from any system running the script.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, whenever the Bash Uploader script is executed (typically during CI/CD pipeline runs)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects all environment variables and git remote configuration, then exfiltrates this data via an HTTP POST request to a hardcoded external IP address (104.248.94.23), resulting in unauthorized disclosure of credentials and secrets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The snippet exfiltrates sensitive environment variables and repository information to an external, non-Codecov IP address without user knowledge or consent, which is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: The legitimate Codecov Bash Uploader is only expected to upload code coverage data to official Codecov servers. It should never transmit environment variables, secrets, or repository configuration to untrusted third-party IP addresses.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may upload coverage reports to trusted endpoints, but never environment variables or secrets to unknown or hardcoded IP addresses. Exfiltration of such data is not required for normal operation.
key_indicators: Presence of a hardcoded external IP address (104.248.94.23) in a Bash script
Use of curl to POST environment variables and git configuration outside normal workflow
No user notification or documentation for this network activity
Collection and transmission of all environment variables and git remotes
Network request destination does not match official Codecov infrastructure

attack_chain.action: A backdoored version of the Codecov Bash Uploader is distributed to users and integrated into their CI/CD pipelines.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious Bash Uploader script during automated CI/CD runs.

attack_chain.action: When the Bash Uploader script runs, it executes the malicious curl command embedded in the script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection and exfiltration of all environment variables and git remote information from the CI/CD environment.

attack_chain.action: The collected sensitive data (including credentials, tokens, and secrets) is sent to the attacker's server at 104.248.94.23.
attack_chain.leads_to: The attacker gains unauthorized access to secrets, enabling further compromise of user environments and potential lateral movement.

behavioral_signatures: Bash scripts executed in CI/CD environments making outbound HTTP requests to hardcoded, non-standard IP addresses
Exfiltration of environment variables or git configuration via network requests in build or deployment scripts
Unexpected use of curl or similar tools to transmit sensitive data to unknown endpoints
file_indicators: Presence of curl commands with hardcoded IP addresses (e.g., 104.248.94.23) in Bash scripts
Modifications to the Codecov Bash Uploader script that do not match official Codecov releases (hash mismatch or unauthorized code additions)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to 104.248.94.23/upload/v2 from CI/CD runners
Unusual network traffic from build environments to unknown or unapproved IP addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Bash scripts in CI/CD environments that make outbound network requests to hardcoded IP addresses, especially those that POST environment variables or git configuration. Compare the hash of the Codecov Bash Uploader script against known-good versions to detect unauthorized modifications. Alert on any script that attempts to exfiltrate environment variables or secrets to non-approved endpoints, and flag any network traffic from CI/CD runners to 104.248.94.23.
